findings.claim: For natural gas, low inventory is associated with higher volatility especially in scarcity and winter states, rather than as a universal linear relation.
findings.expected_direction: below-normal inventory in winter -> higher volatility

findings.claim: Natural-gas forward-curve shape contains information about physical scarcity and inventory state; after seasonal structure is accounted for, tighter inventories are associated with a stronger nearby scarcity signal in the curve rather than a universal linear convenience-yield coefficient.
findings.expected_direction: lower inventory -> stronger nearby-relative-price / backwardation scarcity signal

sources.scope: direct oil-and-natural-gas evidence linking forward-curve shape, scarcity, inventory and volatility

related_sources.scope: direct energy-commodity evidence including Henry Hub on seasonal convenience-yield dynamics inferred from futures prices

findings.design_implication: Reproduce the inventory/curve scarcity relationship directly from exact Henry Hub contract curves and storage state. Do not require an unobserved storage-cost series or label a futures-curve proxy as an exactly observed convenience yield.

findings.claim: U.S. natural-gas futures prices respond inversely to weekly storage-change surprises (actual minus pre-release expected change); the surprise contains information beyond the absolute announcement magnitude.
findings.expected_direction: larger-than-expected build -> lower futures price; larger-than-expected withdrawal -> higher futures price
findings.reproduction_requirement: Requires a historically fixed pre-release consensus or separately justified PIT expectation benchmark; storage actuals alone do not reproduce the published surprise construct.

findings.claim: U.S. natural-gas market dynamics are nonlinear in underground-storage state; structural shock responses are stronger in low-inventory environments and spot-futures relationships differ by inventory regime.
findings.expected_direction: low inventory -> larger price response to shocks
findings.design_implication: Treat storage state as a conditioning variable rather than assuming one linear storage coefficient. Announcement timing and trader-attention effects are owned by line 007 and may be cross-referenced by storage designs without duplicating the finding here.
